reasons: The cited text (Section 12.2(a)(i), captioned 'Termination by Sanofi for Convenience') gives our party (Sanofi, the in-licensing/paying party) an at-will termination right in its entirety and on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis, with no early-termination fee or penalty identified in the effects provision (12.3(c)), which is the preferred T4C position.

RevMed's (counterparty's) termination rights in the cited paragraphs are all cause-based (competing product, cessation of development, with notice/meet-and-discuss/cure mechanics), and 12.2(b)-(c) are breach/insolvency triggers — no counterparty convenience right during the Term, consistent with the preferred position.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is an alias-matching artefact: the clause uses the party name 'Sanofi' rather than a generic Customer/Licensee alias, and the heading expressly says 'for Convenience'. Not substantive.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the redacted notice periods ([***]) are properly noted as an unverifiable sub-element in the rationale rather than escalated to a deviation, in line with the classification semantics.
